A 55-year-old male patient was admitted for acute Gross Hydronephrosis (GH) caused by a kidney stone obstructing the junction of the ureter and renal pelvis. He also had an established renal cell transitional cell carcinoma (T2N0M0), presenting with abdominal girth increase, distension, intermittent nausea, and intractable hiccups. The patient's medical history included hypertension and electrolyte imbalance. Diagnostic imaging confirmed these findings, including a kidney stone and a mass lesion. Laparoscopy and open simple nephrectomy were performed to address both the obstruction and the tumor. Post-surgery, the patient experienced relief from hiccups and improved appetite. Follow-up instructions consisted of dietary modifications and regular follow-up appointments with the healthcare professional.

The patient has been diagnosed with sinusitis and a spinal cord tumor, specifically a dermoid cyst, as confirmed by histopathology. The patient underwent a dorsal D1 to D8 laminectomy, along with a mid-line myelotomy and total tumor excision. Intra-operative and post-operative methylprednisolone was administered. An MRI revealed a large intramedullary cystic lesion in the dorsal spinal cord, consistent with the diagnosis of a dermoid cyst. The patient experienced mild left lower limb weakness post-operatively, which resolved by the 10th post-operative day. The patient is being prescribed methylprednisolone and is scheduled for a follow-up in 10 days to monitor for symptoms.
